pairs.subject: conditional-service-composition
pairs.evidence: src/athena/connectors/spec.py:263 The context loads a flat set of independent connector specs (two builtin JSON files, plus up to 16 MCP servers from one mcp.json) and refuses a duplicate id instead of layering it. There is no multi-service topology, no integration fragment that applies only when two connectors are both present, no host-capability probe and no later-wins merge, so the subject's precondition does not hold; a search of src/athena/connectors, src/athena/daemon and tests/connectors for conjunction, topology, accelerator, docker and specificity found nothing.

techniques.evidence: src/athena/connectors/spec.py:266 Each spec stands alone and is keyed by id; a second document for the same id is refused, not layered. No fragment is selected by a combination of handles.

src/athena/connectors/spec.py:259 The set is discovered by glob, but the result is a dict of disjoint specs with no order-dependent merge, so no layering order is needed (the sorted glob keeps loading deterministic anyway).

src/athena/connectors/health.py:3 Here 'probe' means checking a credential against the provider, not observing what the host can do. No requested and observed tokens share a namespace, and there is no wildcard.
src/athena/connectors/mcp/config.py:143 MCP servers are an explicit list a person writes; no server declares that it requires another, so there is nothing to close over before selection.
